# Platform settings · Mail

## Mail service

<a id="SMTPProvider"></a>

### Mail service preset

Key `SMTPProvider` · Type string · Default `empty` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Mail › Mail service

Which preset the mail service in use was set up from, such as resend, ses, gmail or custom. It only shapes the console form; sending reads the server, port and account. Like every SMTP setting it mirrors the mail service in use and changes with it.

See also: [SMTP server](./mail.md#SMTPServer)

Guide: [deployment/env.md#mail-sending](../deployment/env.md#mail-sending)

<a id="SMTPServer"></a>

### SMTP server

Key `SMTPServer` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Mail › Mail service

The host name of the SMTP server every email is sent through. It mirrors the mail service in use: add, edit or switch services on the Mail services card. Empty means the site cannot send mail, so login codes, password resets and quota warnings stop. When the deployment sets smtp.url (SMTP_URL), that wins and the console is read-only.

Examples:

- `smtp.resend.com` Mail goes out through Resend.

See also: [SMTP port](./mail.md#SMTPPort) · [Encryption](./mail.md#SMTPTLSMode) · [SMTP username](./mail.md#SMTPAccount)

Guide: [deployment/env.md#mail-sending](../deployment/env.md#mail-sending)

<a id="SMTPPort"></a>

### SMTP port

Key `SMTPPort` · Type int · Range 1–65535 · Default `587`

Where: Platform settings › Mail › Mail service

The port of the SMTP server: usually 465 for SSL/TLS and 587 for STARTTLS. With encryption Auto the port decides the encryption, and port 587 logs in with LOGIN instead of PLAIN. It mirrors the mail service in use.

Examples:

- `465` With Auto, the connection is TLS from the first byte.
- `587` With Auto, the connection must upgrade with STARTTLS and logs in with LOGIN.
- `25` With Auto, STARTTLS is still required; pick STARTTLS if offered for a relay without TLS.

See also: [Encryption](./mail.md#SMTPTLSMode) · [SMTP server](./mail.md#SMTPServer)

<a id="SMTPAccount"></a>

### SMTP username

Key `SMTPAccount` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Mail › Mail service

The user name the mail service logs in to the SMTP server with; for a mailbox it is the mailbox address. When no sender address is set, mail is sent from it. It mirrors the mail service in use.

See also: [SMTP password](./mail.md#SMTPToken) · [Sender address](./mail.md#SMTPFrom)

<a id="SMTPFrom"></a>

### Sender address

Key `SMTPFrom` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Mail › Mail service

The address every email comes from. It must be an address the service lets you send from: one on a domain you verified with it, or the mailbox itself. It mirrors the mail service in use.

Examples:

- `noreply@example.com` Users get mail from noreply@example.com; example.com must be verified with the service.

See also: [Sender name](./mail.md#SMTPFromName) · [Reply-to address](./mail.md#SMTPReplyTo)

<a id="SMTPFromName"></a>

### Sender name

Key `SMTPFromName` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Mail › Mail service

The display name shown before the sender address. Empty shows the address alone. It mirrors the mail service in use.

Examples:

- `Example AI` Mail comes from Example AI <noreply@example.com>.

See also: [Sender address](./mail.md#SMTPFrom) · [Site name](./site.md#SystemName)

<a id="SMTPReplyTo"></a>

### Reply-to address

Key `SMTPReplyTo` · Type string · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Mail › Mail service

Where replies to the site's emails go instead of the sender address. Empty sends replies to the sender address. It mirrors the mail service in use.

Examples:

- `support@example.com` A user who replies to a login code email writes to support@example.com.

See also: [Sender address](./mail.md#SMTPFrom)

<a id="SMTPToken"></a>

### SMTP password

Key `SMTPToken` · Type secret · secret: never shown after saving

Where: Platform settings › Mail › Mail service

The password, app password or API key the mail service logs in with. It is never shown again after saving and is encrypted in the database when ENCRYPTION_KEY is set. It mirrors the mail service in use.

See also: [SMTP username](./mail.md#SMTPAccount)

<a id="SMTPTLSMode"></a>

### Encryption

Key `SMTPTLSMode` · Type enum · Default `auto`

Where: Platform settings › Mail › Mail service

How the connection to the SMTP server is encrypted. Auto picks by port and suits almost every service. It mirrors the mail service in use.

Values:

- `auto` Auto (by port): SSL/TLS on port 465, required STARTTLS on any other port.
- `ssl` SSL/TLS: TLS from the first byte, usually on port 465.
- `starttls` STARTTLS (required): Upgrades to TLS after connecting; sending fails when the server cannot.
- `starttls_opportunistic` STARTTLS if offered: Upgrades when the server offers it, otherwise sends in plain text.
- `none` None: Plain text, for a relay on a trusted local network or for development.

See also: [SMTP port](./mail.md#SMTPPort)

## Email templates

<a id="MailTemplates"></a>

### Email templates

Key `MailTemplates` · Type json · Default `empty`

Where: Platform settings › Mail › Email templates

Your own subject and body for each email users get, per console language. The emails are the verification code, password reset, low balance and quota used up. Stored as JSON {"<template>": {"<language>": {"subject", "body"}}}; a template or language left out, or an empty subject or body, uses the built-in text of that language. Variables are a name in double curly braces, HTML-escaped in the body; the server adds the shared header with the logo and the footer. Unknown templates or languages are refused on save.

Examples:

- `{"verification":{"en_US":{"subject":"Your {{site}} code","body":""}}}` English verification emails get the new subject and keep the built-in body; every other email stays built-in.

See also: [Default language](./site.md#DefaultLanguage) · [Site name](./site.md#SystemName) · [Logo URL](./site.md#Logo) · [Quota warning emails](./billing.md#QuotaRemindEnabled)
